messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the canary rollout at ~10:15 we saw ~2.4% of production users still hitting the canary hours after rollback. split metrics show 0% canary configured. this looks like sticky/affinity leak.
jen: oh no, timeline? did we rotate any salts or change header normalization around the same time?
deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary v2024.11.07-rc2 -> 10% at 2024-11-07T10:15:21Z
sasha: I pulled traces for the affected requests, and almost all have missing cookie but have x-client-id header present. many are from our mobile proxy pool.
marco: sounds like header-based routing accidentally got higher precedence than cookie affinity in the new config. i remember a config reorder PR landed yesterday (edge: prefer header guards).
irene: iirc that PR changed normalization rules too (lowercasing + trim). if the client sends mixed-case header it might bypass header guard and then fall back to hash-based sticky which uses old salt -> mismatch -> service returns canary.
alex: attaching the relevant route snippet i checked:
```
route {
  split: { stable: 0.9, canary: 0.1 }
  guards: [
    { type: "header", name: "x-fe-client", match: "^mobile-.*", precedence: 20 },
    { type: "cookie_affinity", cookie_name: "rwd_aff", salt_version: 3 }
  ]
}
```
alex: The problem: when header normalization changed, some proxies started sending X-Fe-Client vs x-fe-client; the new normalizer lowercases but the precedence compare happened before normalization. so header guard didn't fire and cookie_affinity then used a deprecated salt algorithm for certain sessions.
jen: confirm: salt rotated 2 releases ago, but old salted cookies still accepted by stable runtime. canary runtime treats old salt as opaque -> falls back to hashing mismatch -> routing ends up using last-resort route which is canary?
marco: yep. root cause: guard evaluation order uses raw header key for precedence checks, but cookie parsing applies canonicalization later. bug introduced in edge-config ordering patch.
irene: mitigations: 1) hotfix edge to run canonicalization before guard precedence check (low risk) 2) forced reissue of affinity cookies via header on next response (more invasive) 3) temporal traffic reweight to stable via rollout API.
sasha: telemetry: sample ids: trace ids 01ab.., all from region-us-west2 and 92% mobile proxy. good to scope blast radius.
alex: i've put an emergency rollback of the config reorder into a patch branch. can someone approve a quick hotfix for canonicalization-first? @jen @marco
jen: approving, please include tests for header-case-insensitivity in guard unit tests. also add a telemetry counter for "guard_eval_before_normalize" so we can detect recurrence.
rollouts-bot: rollout action queued: hotfix-edge-canonicalize -> staging -> canary -> prod (manual promote)
marco: i'll push the patch now and add an integration test that simulates mixed-case headers + old-cookies.
irene: follow-up: create ENG-1147 to audit other guard types (ip, geo) for canonicalization ordering. also add dashboard panel to show split vs sticky hit rate by client header presence.
alex: created ENG-1147 and a quick dashboard card request (cc @sasha). thanks all. :thumbsup:
